name: Marcelo Bielsa
scopeNote: Manager profile of Marcelo Bielsa across eight counted spells: Newell's Old Boys (1990-07-01 to 1992-06-30), Velez Sarsfield (1997-07-01 to 1998-06-30), Argentina (1998-10-20 to 2004-09-15), Chile (2007-07-11 to 2011-02-04), Athletic Club (2011-07-07 to 2013-06-30), Marseille (2014-05-17 to 2015-08-08), Leeds United (2018-06-15 to 2022-02-27) and Uruguay (2023-05-15 to 2026-06-30). Dates are from the managerial statistics table of English Wikipedia (as of 2026-06-30), cross-checked with Spanish Wikipedia; the two differ in places (see openQuestions). Style named by the evidence: a man-oriented, high-intensity pressing side ('Each outfielder aggressively tracks their opponent', Coaches' Voice 2021; 'a lot of man-marking', The False 9 2020; 'marcar hombre a hombre', Ugarte 2023) built on a 3-3-1-3 (3-4-3 for Argentina 2002) that becomes a 4-1-4-1 / 4-2-3-1 / 4-3-3 when defending or at Leeds and Uruguay, with fast vertical play, attacking wide midfielders or full-backs, rotations and third-man runs. Bielsa himself says the formation drawing matters little ('sobrevalorada la observacion de los esquemas', 2003) and that his teams try to 'protagonizar, atacar, jugar en campo rival, no especular' (2023). Evolution: Newell's, Argentina and Chile played a back three with four or three forwards; at Athletic and Marseille the base was reported as a back three/four hybrid; Leeds and Uruguay start from a back four with a single pivot dropping between centre-backs. Marking: the evidence for man-oriented defending is strong at Athletic (2012), Marseille (2014), Leeds (2018-22) and Uruguay (2023-24), and weak or missing for the 1990s teams. Facts from excluded spells were not used as evidence.

spellsCounted.reason: Primera Division 1990-91 and Clausura 1992, Copa Libertadores runner-up 1992 (Wikipedia); 97 matches; players of the era describe a tactically drilled, aggressive-recovery team (ESPN 2022). Where his 3-3-1-3 started.
Clausura 1998 title (44 matches); Chilavert recalls the verticality he imposed. Thin tactical coverage, counted on the title test.
85 matches; 2002 World Cup 3-4-3 with documented tactical coverage; Copa America 2004 runner-up and Olympic gold 2004 (Argentina U23) in the same cycle; later move to bigger jobs.
51 matches; 2010 World Cup round of 16 with the 3-3-1-3 and wide attacking play; the style Chile kept after him.
113 matches; Europa League and Copa del Rey finals 2012; the pressing and man-marking team that beat Manchester United 5-3 on aggregate.

41 matches; StatsBomb ranked its press among the most aggressive in the big five leagues; recognisable style with tactical coverage even though no title and a resignation after the first match of 2015/16.
170 matches; EFL Championship 2019/20 and promotion, then the Premier League; the best-documented spell, with a man-marking 4-1-4-1 / 3-3-1-3 and a famous press.

39 matches; Copa America 2024 third place (Wikipedia; one paywalled TFA piece says fourth); strong first-hand accounts of man-to-man marking and pressing. Wikipedia shows the departure made official on 2026-06-30, so the spell is closed.

spellsExcluded.reason: 77 matches, no titles, and no tactical coverage found (no analysis in English or Spanish was read). Dates from English Wikipedia; Spanish Wikipedia gives 1992-1994. Fails the 'known for' test as researched.
33 matches (10 W, 14 D, 9 L), no titles, no tactical coverage found; left in March 1996. Fails the 'known for' test.
12 matches (3 W, 3 D, 6 L), left to take the Argentina job; no titles and too short for a style to be documented.
Appointed 2016-07-05 and resigned 2016-07-08 (English Wikipedia; Spanish Wikipedia says confirmed 2016-07-06 and out two days later). No match played, so no evidence at all.
14 matches (3 W, 4 D, 7 L), suspended 2017-11-22 and contract ended 2017-12-15 (Spanish Wikipedia). Below the ~15-match minimum, no titles, and no analysis of the Lille team was read.

openQuestions: Marking (mar): all verified man-marking evidence is from Athletic (2012), Marseille (2014), Leeds (2018-22) and Uruguay (2023-24). For Newell's, Velez, Argentina and Chile no source says whether defending was zonal or man-oriented (Chile 2010: only 'each player in a personal duel with an opponent', Sports Illustrated, ambiguous). Bielsa himself was not found explaining his marking in an interview. Confirm whether the audit should treat the whole career as man-oriented or weight the later spells.

Seven spells share almost no evidence on some dimensions. Counted spells weigh the same, but Velez (one Chilavert quote), Argentina (one 2002 study) and Chile (one 2010 piece) are thin against Leeds and Uruguay.

Dates differ between English and Spanish Wikipedia: Atlas 1993-95 vs 1992-94; Chile start 2007-07-11 vs 2007-08-10; Athletic end 2013-06-30 (table) vs club non-renewal confirmed 2013-06-07; Argentina and Velez end dates are only in the English table. English table dates were used throughout.

Atlas and Club America were excluded for lack of tactical coverage and titles, not because the match counts are short (77 and 33). If Mexican-language sources show a recognisable style there, they could be counted.
Lille 2017 (14 matches) is just under the ~15-match minimum and was excluded; a Lille analysis could show the same press as Marseille and Leeds.
Uruguay: the user's task listed the spell as '2023-'; Wikipedia shows the departure made official on 2026-06-30, so it was closed. Confirm.

Style change inside the profile: three-forward 3-3-1-3 / 3-4-3 in the 1990s and 2000s vs a back four with a single pivot at Leeds and Uruguay; Athletic and Marseille sources disagree on back three vs back four (a French analysis of PSG-OM 2014 reads Marseille as a 4-2-3-1 with individual marking, StatsBomb reports mid-season intensity 'tapered off').

Athletic 2011-13: pressing and man-marking are only supported by one tier C retrospective (Planet Football 2025, 'almost militaristic man-marking' v Manchester United, March 2012), one Bleacher Report review of the April 2012 Sporting tie, and Ferguson's quote. No Spielverlagerung or TFA analysis of that team was found.

Stated views: Bielsa's own statements on marking, pressing and his formation come from press (2003, 2011, 2012, 2019, 2023, 2024). The 1991 El Grafico interview 'Yo miro videos para atacar, no para defender' (403) could be the earliest primary source for his attacking priority; not read.
The Wikipedia pages were read only to character 100000 of about 233000 (English) and 325000 (Spanish).
Search summaries claimed that at Velez only three starters were not from the club's academy; that was not on any page read and is not used.

confidence.reason: Leeds (2018-22) is covered by several tier A-B analyses that agree (Coaches' Voice 2021, TFA 2019, TheMastermindSite 2020, StatsBomb for Marseille 2014) on a man-oriented high press, 3-3-1-3 / 4-1-4-1 and wide attacking play, and Uruguay has first-hand player accounts of man-to-man marking. Kept at medium because the 1990s and 2000s spells (Newell's, Velez, Argentina, Chile), which count the same as Leeds, rest on one or two tier C pieces each, mostly retrospective; Athletic marking rests on a retrospective and one match review; the Wikipedia pages were read only in part; and Bielsa's own words on his marking were not found. Every dimension and axis has at least one verified fact, but many are one article from a single spell.
